newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Inter-Continental opens hotel in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Inter-Continental opens hotel in Cambodia.

text.p: Inter-Continental Hotels and Resorts added to its global empire on Thursday with the soft opening of a 15-storey luxury hotel in Cambodia's capital.

Tourism Minister Veng Sereyvudh signed in as the first guest at the five-star Hotel Inter-Continental Phnom Penh, which will start operations with around 100 of its rooms completed and a staff of 502 from 21 countries.

It will play host over the next week to more than 100 dignitaries attending the South East Asian Biennial Film Festival, the hotel's staff said, adding that 354 rooms would be ready for occupancy by the time of the grand opening in September.
"We're looking at 50 percent occupancy for this year and in the next five years, we are looking for occupancy going up to 70 percent," said hotel general manager Thierry Douin.
The hotel was built at a cost of around $60 million and is being managed by the Japanese-owned Inter-Continental group under a 10-year contract.
The hotel's rooms start at a special introductory rate of $120 for a standard deluxe room.

Marcello Pigozzo, Inter-Continental's group president for the Asia Pacific region, said the hotel's main competition was expected to come from the Singapore-based Raffles group, which is expected to open the renovated 70-year-old Royale Hotel later this year.
Inter-Continental, one of the world's largest privately owned luxury hotel chains, is owned by the Tokyo-based Saison Group and has more than 190 hotels worldwide.
